keyVerseText: Of the sons of Bani; Maadai, Amram, and Uel,
rootMeaning: The Hebrew name אוּאֵל (ʼÛwʼêl) is etymologically composed of two parts: אוֹ (ʼôw), which can mean 'or,' 'also,' or imply desire, and אֵל (El), meaning 'God.' Together, the name conveys the sense of 'wish of God' or 'will of God.' This root meaning highlights a personal connection to divine intent or purpose, emphasizing that the bearer of the name is closely associated with God's sovereign will rather than a generic human desire.
usageInScripture: The name Uel appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Ezra 10:34, where it is listed among the sons of Bani. The translation 'and Uel' indicates that it is used as a proper name without additional descriptive meaning in context. This singular occurrence suggests the name identifies a specific individual whose identity is tied to the meaning 'will of God,' reflecting a personal and covenantal relationship rather than a broad thematic usage.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Uel as 'will of God' enriches our appreciation of biblical names as carriers of divine purpose and identity. In the Christian faith, names that incorporate 'El' remind believers of God's active presence and sovereign will in the lives of His people. This name, borne by a Judean during the exile period, points to God's sustaining will even amid hardship and covenant challenges. It encourages believers to see their own identities as shaped by God's sovereign desire and faithfulness, inviting trust in His providential guidance.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 10:34 lists Uel among the sons of Bani, emphasizing his identity within the restored community of Israel after exile. The inclusion of Uel here, whose name means 'will of God,' subtly underscores that even in the act of restoration, God's sovereign will is at work in the individuals who make up His people. This reminds readers that God’s purposes are fulfilled through real people, called by names that declare His presence and intention.
